title: Smoking, vaping and alcohol
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T14:56:01Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point covers shared risk factors for chronic disease in general, not the specific burden of tobacco, vaping and alcohol on Australian cancers, heart disease and injury that the new point needs.

draft.title: Smoking, vaping and alcohol
card: Burden of disease is the total harm a health problem causes, through both early death and years lived with illness or disability. Tobacco, vaping and alcohol each add to it in Australia.
Tobacco
Smoking is a major cause of many cancers, especially lung cancer. It also damages blood vessels and the heart, so it raises the risk of heart disease.
Vaping
Vapes deliver nicotine, which is addictive, and other chemicals into the lungs. Young people who vape are more likely to go on to smoke.
Alcohol
Alcohol raises the risk of some cancers and heart disease. It also causes injury, because it slows reactions and judgement, for example in road crashes and falls.
draft.remember: Tobacco, vaping and alcohol add to the burden of disease, and alcohol adds injury as well as illness.

a.q: Which pair of health effects is linked to both tobacco use and alcohol use?
opts: Cancers and heart disease
Injury and lung cancer
Heart disease and road crashes
Cancers and addiction to nicotine
a.why: The card links both tobacco and alcohol to cancers and heart disease. Injury is linked to alcohol because it slows reactions and judgement, not to tobacco. Nicotine addiction comes from tobacco and vapes, not alcohol.
a.clue: Find the harms the card names under both Tobacco and Alcohol.

b.q: Liam, 19, has a few drinks at a party in Geelong and then falls down the stairs and breaks his arm. Which part of alcohol's effect on the burden of disease does this show?
opts: Injury, as alcohol slows reactions and judgement
Cancer, as alcohol damages cells over many years
Heart disease, as alcohol damages blood vessels
Addiction, as alcohol delivers nicotine to the body
b.why: A fall soon after drinking is an injury, and alcohol causes injury by slowing reactions and judgement. Cancer and heart disease are also linked to alcohol, but they are illnesses that build up over time, so they do not fit a single fall.
b.clue: Think about what happened straight after the drinks, not years later.

b.best: Injury, as alcohol slows reactions and judgement

problems.detail: The card defines 'burden of disease', a term that belongs to point 1 (Australia's health status, where cancers, heart disease and mental health conditions lead the burden of disease). This point should only mention it, not define it.

proposal.title: Smoking, vaping and alcohol
card: Tobacco, vaping and alcohol are behavioural risk factors: things people do that raise their risk of poor health. Each adds to Australia's burden of disease.
Tobacco
Smoking is a major cause of many cancers, especially lung cancer. It also damages blood vessels and the heart, so it raises the risk of heart disease.
Vaping
Vapes deliver nicotine, which is addictive, and other chemicals into the lungs. Young people who vape are more likely to go on to smoke.
Alcohol
Over many years, alcohol raises the risk of some cancers and heart disease. It can also cause injury straight away, because it slows reactions and judgement, for example in road crashes and falls.
proposal.remember: Tobacco and alcohol both raise the risk of cancers and heart disease. Alcohol can also cause injury, and vapes add nicotine addiction.

a.q: Which pair of health effects is linked to both tobacco use and alcohol use?
opts: Cancers and heart disease
Injury and lung cancer
Heart disease and road crashes
Cancers and addiction to nicotine
a.why: Both tobacco and alcohol raise the risk of cancers and heart disease. Injury, such as road crashes, comes from alcohol slowing reactions and judgement, not from tobacco. Nicotine addiction comes from tobacco and vapes, not alcohol.
a.clue: Look for harms shared by smoking and drinking.

opts: Injury, as alcohol slows reactions and judgement

Heart disease, as alcohol damages blood vessels
Addiction, as alcohol delivers nicotine to the body
b.why: A fall soon after drinking is an injury, and alcohol can cause injury by slowing reactions and judgement. Cancer and heart disease are also linked to alcohol, but their risk builds up over many years, so they do not fit a single fall.
b.clue: Think about what happened straight after the drinks, not years later.
